_notes: Taito do Brasil Oba-Oba (1980) on the later hardware: the 1979 firmware moved up to the 0x4000 window. It keeps
the 1979 structure - credits display at 0x408F, player count at 0x408D - but puts settings, high score and stored
credits where the 1981-85 boards do (0x4070, 0x4079, 0x407F). Compiled 2026-10 by evilwraith from the ROM code
only (the LDA 407F / STA 408F credits copy, the settings DAA check over 0x4070-0x4079, the 0x4079 high-score
compare, the replay routine, the game-over write); no image or live capture yet. No current_player is declared:
the 1979 firmware's equivalent byte has not been identified.
Display scores are three BCD bytes least-significant first (platform endian: little); 0xFF 0xFF 0xFF is a blank
display. The nine-byte BCD settings block is edited from the service menu and validated at reset (a non-BCD byte
restores all nine from ROM); balls per game is its first byte and the three replay levels its fifth to seventh.
No checksum. The firmware deliberately resumes a game in progress at reset; PinMAME's taito driver (2026-10)
marks the saved game over on load so a table starts in attract.

player_count._notes: 1979-style: the reset path refuses to resume with 5 or more here. Code only; not yet seen live.
player_count.label: Players

credits._notes: Stored value; the firmware keeps a display copy at 0x408F.
credits.label: Credits

match._notes: Match digit shown after the game; cycles 0-9 during play (the randomiser).
match.label: Match

game_over._notes: Bit 0 of the firmware's flags byte: set in attract and by its reset path when it declines to resume, clear during a game.
game_over.label: Game Over

score._notes: Most-significant byte first, unlike the display; the reset path reloads it from the ROM's minimum if it reads lower.

02.label: Replay Level 1
02._notes: One BCD byte compared against the two most-significant digits of the score (x10,000). A level equal to the one before it is skipped, so 30 30 30 is a single replay at 300,000. The same routine in every set.
